cards.text: The people have gone back to work on the house of the LORD. Then, on the twenty-first day of the seventh month, the word of the LORD comes through Haggai the prophet. He's to speak to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, to Joshua, the high priest, and to the remnant of the people.
God gives Haggai a question to ask them, and it starts like this: "Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory?"

cards.question: Next to its former glory, how does God ask if this house looks to the people now?

cards.text: That question stings like a buddy pulling up your photos from ten years ago, going, "Wow. Look at you back THEN." But God doesn't leave them sitting in that, and He has a word for the governor, for the high priest and for all the people of the land.

cards.question: God speaks to Zerubbabel, to Joshua the high priest and to all the people of the land. What does He tell each of them?
Then God tells them to ___, because He is with them.

cards.text: Then God reaches back into Israel's history. He says this is a promise He already made to them once.

cards.question: God says He made this promise at a big moment in Israel's history. Which moment?

answers.text: When they came out of Egypt

cards.question: God tells the people that His Spirit remains among them, and He tells them not to be afraid.

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts looks ahead. He says that once more, in a little while, He's going to shake things.

cards.question: When the LORD of Hosts says He will shake things once more, how much does He say He will shake?

answers.text: Heavens and earth and sea and land
Just the walls of the city

cards.question: God says He will shake all the nations, and they will come with all their armies.

cards.text: Not armies, friend. TREASURES. All the nations come with all their treasures.

cards.question: God asked if this house seemed like nothing. Now He says He will fill this house with ___.
The nations come with their treasures. Whose does the LORD of Hosts say the silver and the gold are?
God says the latter glory of this house will be smaller than the former.
And in this place, God says He will provide ___.

findings.problem: Most story cards have little or none of Papa Dorin's voice. Cards 1, 2, 7 and 10 are plain retellings with no reaction, comparison, disbelief or self-deprecation. Card 4 is the only real joke, and card 13 has the only LOUD beat. The walkthrough reads like a pleasant summary, not laugh-out-loud Papa Dorin.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The opening card is a flat list of the date and the people being addressed, with no trace of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. It is the only sweeping, four-part answer, and both wrong answers are small, limited places that start with "Just" or "Only." Card 10 already says the LORD of Hosts will shake things, so the baker can pick the big answer without understanding the verse. The wrong answers are also vague places rather than the same kind of thing as heavens, earth, sea and dry land.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The wrong answers "Just the walls of the city" and "Only the hills around Judah" make the right answer stand out by contrast.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The story card has three sentences: "Not armies, friend." "TREASURES." "All the nations come with all their treasures."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "The nations'" can be argued as right. Haggai 2:7 says the nations "will come with all their treasures," and the question itself says "The nations come with their treasures." A baker could reasonably say the silver and gold are the nations'. The wrong answer is not false everywhere in the passage.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: "The nations'" is close to a near-match with the passage's own wording about "their treasures."

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
